newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds slightly up, boosted by peso issue.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds slightly up, boosted by peso issue.

text.p: Argentine bonds were slightly higher late morning Thursday in slim trade after the announcement of a five-year peso bond.
"The market is very calm," said a trader at a local brokerage house.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was up 1/8 at 93-7/8 while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 4 due 2002 was up $0.10 at 117.90.

The announcement of a five-year peso bond issue to be priced at between 240 and 245 basis points over U.S. Treasuries was seen supporting local instruments. Rumors of the issue, which is lead managed by Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, led to gains in peso bonds Wednesday.
The indicated spread level for the bond gave yet more evidence of falling country risk, when compared with the similarly-dated domestic Bonte Treasury bond denominated in dollars, traders said.
That bond, maturing in May 2002, was trading at a spread of 228 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.

Players said the market shrugged off the resignation of Justice Minister Elias Jassan. Jassan offered his resignation earlier in the week because of contacts with a businessman suspected in a murder case and alleged to be a mobster.
The government said Thursday it had accepted Jassan's resignation, adding that he will be replaced with the current ambassador to Washington, Raul Granillo Ocampo.
"The market is not very worried about it," said another trader. Rather, it remains focussed on next week's meeting of the rate-setting U.S. Federal Open Market Committee.
